description:
## What

`Fetcher::URLValidator` has two methods for URL validation that disagree:

- `valid?(url : String?) : Bool`: returns false for nil/empty/relative/invalid-URL. Uses `ALLOWED_SCHEMES = {"http", "https"}` whitelist.
- `safe_scheme?(url : String?) : Bool`: returns TRUE for nil/empty/relative URLs. Uses `DANGEROUS_SCHEMES` blacklist (`javascript`, `vbscript`, `data`, etc.).

The two methods have different rules. `valid?` blocks relative URLs ("comments/123" returns false). `safe_scheme?` allows them ("comments/123" returns true).

## Why

Two validation paths with different rules. Code that uses one might be vulnerable to what the other would block. `entry_factory.cr` uses `safe_scheme?` for secondary URLs (sanitize_secondary_url, sanitize_attachment) and `valid?` for the main URL. The two paths can disagree on edge cases.

There's also a `DANGEROUS_SCHEMES` constant in url_validator.cr that is only consulted by `safe_scheme?`. The main `valid?` path uses `ALLOWED_SCHEMES` whitelist only.

## How

Unify the two methods. Options:

(a) Make `valid?` the single source of truth. Have `safe_scheme?` call `valid?` and return its result (or a less-strict version of it).

(b) Make `safe_scheme?` a strict superset of `valid?`. Add the relative-URL / empty checks to `safe_scheme?` so it never permits what `valid?` blocks.

(c) Delete `safe_scheme?`. `valid?` is sufficient. Update `entry_factory.cr` and the `url_sanitization_spec.cr` to use `valid?`.

(c) is the cleanest. `safe_scheme?` was added for defense-in-depth against `javascript:`-style attacks, but `valid?`'s ALLOWED_SCHEMES whitelist already blocks those schemes.

## Counter-considerations

`safe_scheme?` has separate test coverage in `spec/security/url_sanitization_spec.cr`. If we delete it, those tests need to be updated to use `valid?` (or removed if redundant).

## Done when

- One canonical URL-validation method on URLValidator
- `entry_factory.cr` and any other callers use it
- `spec/security/url_sanitization_spec.cr` is updated or removed
- Full spec suite still green
- `grep -rn 'safe_scheme?' src/ spec/` returns no hits (or only tests for the deletion)
title: Fix: URLValidator.safe_scheme? vs valid? inconsistency
